notes.title: Airborne Empire an open-world city-building RPG gets a Linux / Steam Deck freezing fix
notes.notes:
Airborne Empire is an interesting hybrid that mixes city-building, with open-world exploration and the latest update should fix it up on Linux / Steam Deck.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2025/09/airborne-empire-an-open-world-city-building-rpg-gets-a-linux-steam-deck-freezing-fix/

notes.title: Storms over Tropicos Islands
notes.notes:
[p][/p][p]Hey Everyone,[/p][p]Today we are excited to deliver our [b]biggest update yet to Airborne Empire[/b].
This one is a full on expansion; we’ve added a new biome that comes with new quests and new enemies (Pirate Cruiser, Barrage Balloon and Tractor Beam). We’ve also added a weather system to the game that, while specifically featured in the new region, also impacts the other regions as well. We also added several new buildings (Turbine Engine, Birdcage Bar and Ferris Wheel) and customization options for the player's city. In addition we did a lot of combat tuning based on player feedback and the impact of the new enemies. Many bugs were also fixed!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/77cf2bddb3fce80e15c6b9ba088bf8c820c2f47a.jpg"][/img]


To celebrate the occasion, Airborne Empire is currently on its historically lowest discount at 30% off:
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2438680/Airborne_Empire/"][/dynamiclink]
[/p][h2]New Biome[/h2][p]First, let’s talk about the new biome[b]; The Tropicos Islands[/b]. [/p][p]Normally the Tropicos Islands are a popular vacation destination but lately they’ve been having a tough time. Not only is the area completely overrun by pirates but the weather is also out of control! The entire region has been plagued by never ending storms for months now. Visit the city of Costa Tropicos and unlock a new quest, which will help unravel the mystery of what’s causing the storms and why they won’t stop. There are also a number of side quests available from the new characters you encounter at Costa Tropicos, which is located just West of the Blackspine biome.
[/p][h2]New buildings[/h2][p]We’ve also [b]added a few new buildings[/b] that players can discover and add to their city:[/p][list][*][p][b]The Turbine Engine[/b]: This is a [b]large heavy duty powered turbine that provides a massive amount of Lift[/b] for your city, more than any of the other Lift buildings currently available. It’s a bit of a coal chugger but can, of course, be upgraded and optimized. You can purchase the blueprint for this building from the Academy at Costa Tropicos.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Bird Cage Bar:[/b] A similar building to the Tavern, this building provides [b]Morale[/b] and can be purchased at the Academy at Costa Tropicos.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Ferris Wheel:[/b] Another fun [b]Morale[/b] building that can only be unlocked by finding and completing a hidden quest within the Tropicos Islands biome.[/p][/*][/list][h2]
Combat[/h2][p]Ok, time to talk about Combat. First off, there are [b]two new enemies[/b] that have been added to the game with this update and we’ve also [b]completely reworked how the Pirate Tesla Cannon[/b] works:[/p][list][*][p](New) [b]Barrage Balloon[/b]: Hidden on the ground until a player’s city moves in range. Then the balloon quickly flies to altitude, pulling a cannon up in the air with it. Their strength is the [b]element of surprise[/b]. [/p][/*][*][p](New) [b]Pirate Cruiser[/b]: A [b]Water based ship[/b] with a cannon on board. Constantly moving, but in simple patterns. Players will have to carefully aim their shots to lead their target.[/p][/*][*][p](Redesign) [b]Pirate Tractor Beam[/b]: The Pirate Tesla Cannon is now the Pirate Tractor Beam. It now uses electromagnetism to create a electric burst that [b]pulls the player’s city towards it[/b]. This sets the pirates up to be able to move the player’s city into position where more ground weapons can attack it at once. If the player destroys the Tesla while being pulled their city will immediately stop. I think this creates more interesting gameplay (and compliments the new player cannon range well) and adds a layer of strategy; the player will want to take better stock of how the pirate fortresses are setup, and what the best approach angles and attack priorities are.[/p][/*][/list][p]These two enemies are seen in the new biome but have also been added to the Blackspine and the Desert. These, in combination with our already existing enemy types (and some additional changes to them listed below) have created some very fun and more dynamic combat situations which players can deal with using a variety of strategies. I don’t think we’re done with combat by any means but I think this will open up some fun new strategic choices.[/p][h3]
Combat Tuning Updates:[/h3][list][*][p]The [b]range of the player’s cannon has increased[/b]. A fully upgraded cannon can now outrange the pirate ground cannons, which helps balance out some of the new abilities the pirates have.[/p][/*][*][p]The range of the player’s barrage cannon has also changed. Rather than do massive damage to an area directly beneath it we’ve changed the angle so that [b]it projects that same area damage out in front of it a little more[/b]. This increased range will hopefully make it more viable. It still doesn’t have the range, or recharge rate, of the regular cannon but it can take out multiple targets with one shot, very useful for the more dense pirate setups and against the Tractor Beam.[/p][/*][*][p]The Player Freeze Cannon and Tesla Coil also got some small tuning updates; The [b]Freeze Cannon effect now lasts longer[/b]. The [b]Tesla Coil got a slight range and duration boost[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]A lot of the pirate combat setups in the original three biomes have changed. Many pirate weapons were moved around or added. This means if you already beat the game and you go back there might be a few random enemies floating around. You have to start a new game after this update to really see the new intention for some of the combat setups. That being said, these changes won’t invalidate any saves, it’s just that we changed a bunch of combat encounters that you may have already beat, so you won’t see the changes. Play the game again is what I am really saying… or maybe wait until the next big expansion that will conclude the main story…[/p][/*][/list][h2]
Other Updates and Bug Fixes:[/h2][list][*][p][b]3X speed is now a bit faster[/b] is now truly 3X speed, so you can progress time a little quicker now[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Relic: The Eye of the Valkyrie[/b] - [b]all workers in range of this relic cannot be injured[/b]. Get this Relic by completing the main quest in the Tropicos Islands region.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Achievement[/b] added for completing Tropicos quest line[/p][/*][*][p][b]Allow selecting pirate loot that fell inside forests and other resource mines[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Fixed projectiles hitting their targets less consistently at lower fps and/or faster game speed[/p][/*][*][p]Quick saving now only overwrites quick saves for the same playthrough[/p][/*][*][p][b]Updated the footprint of the Scales of Aelius wonder[/b] to make it more compatible with symmetrical cities[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed rebuild button not working sometimes[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed lift showing up as 0 from buildings in research tree and city academies[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed quest ruins not showing from Orrery after they are mined[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed quest radius not showing in some cases[/p][/*][*][p]Updated FSR 2 version for better upscaling quality on AMD GPUs[/p][/*][/list][p]
This was a long update, thanks for reading. We're looking forward to your feedback!
We would love to see you on our Discord: [url="https://discord.com/invite/sgYxeyu"]https://discord.com/invite/sgYxeyu[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Thanks![/p][p]The Wandering Band[/p][p]
[/p]

Once you update your game on Steam you will have the [b]Summer Theme[/b] available in your building customization menu. Easiest way to activate it is to select your Town Center, click on customize, select the Summer Theme at the top and then click the Apply to All button. 🍉[/p][p][/p][p][b]Get Airborne Empire at a 25% discount[/b] during the Summer Sale! Our biggest discount yet! 🍦🛩️[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2438680/Airborne_Empire/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Over the last couple of weeks we’ve updated the game a few times, mostly with bug fixes and quality of life updates. Some time in the last couple of months we introduced some rare crashes, which we’ve now fixed, and we also got some nice performance improvements in there as well. If you were one of the people who had experienced those crashes we apologize and we also wanted to thank the folks who provided logs and save files to help us track down the issue, we really appreciate the help and support![/p][p]Now that this summer theme pack has released, we are shifting our focus to our next update, which is going to be a big one. As always, if you have any feedback please let us know![/p][p]🏝️🏝️🏝️[/p][p][/p][h3]This update also comes with some [b]bug fixes[/b]:[/h3][list][*][p]Reveal quest ruin icons with Orrery[/p][/*][*][p]Don't scale area circles for quest objectives in map when zooming in and out[/p][/*][*][p]Fix error when changing Shadow quality settings[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/a9f9615384e1cd2c068e328f54821cd83a506e8f.gif"][/img][/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Ancient Wonders Update!
notes.notes:
[h1]Ancient Wonders Update![/h1]
In today’s update we added [b]Wonders[/b] to the game. Wonders are special buildings for your city, you can only have one of each, that provide a unique ability. [b]Each Wonder has a special quest[/b] that needs to be completed to unlock the blueprint. [b]We also added an achievement for unlocking each one.[/b]

[b]The Giving Tree:[/b] This Wonder provides the players city with a [b]constant source of Wood[/b], no workers or planes needed! The quest to unlock it can be found at Litalos, after the player lifts the siege blocking the city. 

[b]The Scales of Aelius:[/b] Once the player builds this Wonder in their city they never have to worry about tilt. No matter how uneven the weight in your city is distributed The Scales of Aelius will [b]always keep you in perfect balance[/b]. This quest can be found in the city of Nassab, once you have helped liberate it.

[b]The Great Orrery:[/b] This Wonder allows the player to immediately [b]see all points of interest on the map[/b], regardless of how much they have explored. Having trouble finding every quest location or settlement? The Great Orrery provides all the answers! The quest to unlock this quest is given at The Watchfort, once the player has helped them rebuild the city.

[b]The Divine Reliquary:[/b] This Wonder [b]houses 1 Relic and that Relic's power will impact the entire city[/b], rather than being limited by the range of the Minaret it is placed in. This one is super powerful and can really be helpful in lots of different situations. The quest to unlock this one can be found at Sainte Verde in The Blackspine.

[h2]This update also comes with bug fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Fixed Settlement UI not showing up when there is a quest on it and all recruits have been hired[/b]
[*] Fixed Tavern and other population providers providing morale after upgrading it even if there are no workers assigned
[*] Fixed Shoot button on building ui remaining grayed out when selecting cannon after shooting other cannon
[*] Fixd rarity indicator not being shown on relic buttons in top bar ui
[*] Fixed "bug unsued" when worker is looting dragon loot
[/list]

notes.title: Quality of Life Update - v0.2.20
notes.notes:
We've listened to a lot of player feedback concerning the UI! So here are a bunch of [b]Quality of Life [/b]features for navigating the game and UI. We wanted to include some of those features at Early Access launch but weren't able to do it in time so here it is!

[h3]Here are some highlights for some of the most requested features:[/h3]
[b][list]
[*] Add buttons next to Recently Destroyed Building bullets to show location of destroyed building and to rebuild destroyed building if possible
[*] Add buttons next to Worker UI bullets to Dismiss all workers, Fully Staff buildings and Select Building (same as clicking the bullet itself)
[*] Allow setting Destination Buoy directly from the Map by right clicking (right click was previously for setting map marker)
[/list][/b]

[h3]Here's a list of other features in this update[/h3]
[list]
[*] Organize Worker UI bullets by building category to more easily find buildings
[*] Keep People UI bullet even if no workers are working on that building type
[*] Allow setting map marker in map by left clicking (previously was right click)
[*] [b]Show quest rewards in the quest info panel[/b]
[*] [b]Show red marker in Compass for current quest[/b]
[*] Make Map Marker and text in map contrast better
[*] Scale icons when zoomed out beyond a certain threshold to make icons more visible when zoomed out
[*] Save Map Marker so it keeps its position when loading save game
[*] Correctly highlight next quest location in map when previous one completes
[*] Add Legend in Map to more clearly communicate the purpose of some icons to the player
[*] [b]Go back to the same camera rotation when coming out of ground city/settlement interaction UI[/b]
[*] Prevent camera from going into settlement UI when player has recruited all workers from settlement.
[*] Don't show Freezing Immunity on non freezable buildings
[*] Move lift required text with the rest of the stats in the selected Building UI
[*] Make backing of most panels more opaque so text is more readable
[*] Hide Update Feed when Research Tree or Map are shown
[*] [b]Keep update feed items much longer[/b]
[*] Make some building descriptions more detailed
[*] Updated some side quest dialogues
[/list]

[h3]Bug fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Fixed home base looping around for nothing sometimes (again!)[/b]
[*] [b]Fixed only some affected buildings being highlighted when selecting minaret or workshop in very large cities[/b]
[*] Fixed "No Relic" button not always at the end of the relics list in the Relic Panel UI
[*] Fixed bug when selecting road in really big cities sometimes
[*] Fixed bug where some buttons would remain highlighted after being clicked
[*] Fixed bug where recently destroyed buildings would still be saved and loaded incorrectly
[*] Fixed light customization showing up on Flame Shrine even though there is no light
[/list]

notes.title: Spring Update! - New Spring Theme Pack and Easy Difficulty
notes.notes:
The [b]Steam Spring Sale[/b] is here and we’ve got a new update for Airborne Empire! We’ve got a few fun things for you in this one:

[b]Spring Theme Pack[/b]: A new Theme Pack that allows you to add Spring themed decorations to your buildings. Cherry blossom trees, hidden Easter Eggs (literally), and some fun spring character balloons! To apply new themes just select your Town Center and open the customization panel.

We’ve also added a couple of [b]new Morale buildings[/b] to the game. 

First up is the [b]Shrine Flame[/b]. This shrine will boost your cities morale score without the need for any workers, just a little bit of Coal each hour to keep that flame burning. 

The other new morale building is the [b]Park[/b]. This building provides Morale with no workers, and instead just uses a little bit of Water.

Lastly, we added an [b]Easy difficulty mode[/b]. We had gotten some feedback that there were some players who just wanted to focus on the city building and story and have less aggressive combat. So we setup a mode where the enemy damage is dialed way back. We still have plans for a Hard difficulty mode but that ones takes a little more time to get right, so stay tuned!

Alright, that's it for this one. We’re already cooking up another fun update for April, we’ll update the Roadmap on our Discord and Steam Forums soon.

Hope you enjoy!

notes.title: High-flying RPG city builder Airborne Empire has launched on Steam, and it's testing my balancing skills in more ways than one
notes.notes: My flying city in Airborne Empire is tilted at a 1 degree angle. That's not a big deal: it's barely detectable visually and it doesn't seem to be bothering my citizens. It sure is bothering me, though. I can't stop imagining one of my residents, after a hard day harvesting resources or battling pirates or working in the iron foundry, coming home, sitting down to relax, placing a pencil on the coffee table in his living room, and watching that pencil slowly roll away... Read more.

notes.title: Flying city-builder Airborne Empire hits early access today with a new military element
notes.notes:
In 2020's Airborne Kingdom, you cobbled together a flying city from sailcloth, smokestacks, wings and flippers, striving to meet a growing population's need for food and shelter while dealing with the more exotic problem of levelling your streets out and generating enough lift. In the process, you explored a beautiful, Orientalist world map of faded mosaic tiles and dusty gold fittings.

In Airborne Empire, out in early access today, you do much the same again, but this time the world is trying to murder you. A bit. You are no longer alone in the skies: there are merchant dirigibles you can barter with, and pirate airships who'll strafe your suburbs and set your bazaars on fire. As such, the sequel's new city technologies include a choice of offensive and defensive weapons. Here's a launch trailer.

Read more

notes.title: September Dev Update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, sorry we haven't done any updates for a while but we're back on it! Going forward I will try to get one out each month. 

First thing I would like to do is address the Early Access Launch Date. We still have not announced a specific date for launch but we are getting very close. Some folks noticed we updated our Steam page to say January 2025. That's the month we are targeting, we don't have a specific day yet but we will announce that ASAP.

We had originally stated our goal was to launch early access this Fall so let me quickly address why we ultimately decided to go for January instead. Anytime there is a big decision like this it is always a combination of things. January gives us more time to fix some crashes that we discovered during the demo. Fred and his wife had their first child in July (yay!) and we wanted him to be able to take more time off, instead of rushing back to try and fix the crashes before launch. A bunch of heavy hitting games, including within the city-builder genre, are coming out this Fall. Its packed! We're a small team and its hard to get discovered on Steam. We are hoping that January is less busy and we are able to have our game featured more.

Last thing I will touch on, since we're already talking about Early Access, is what players should expect from us when Early Access launches: 

The entire city-builder aspect of the game will be complete. We will have all the core buildings (we may still add more later of course) and mechanics that make the city-builder work. You will be able to build glorious flying cities!

The World will have 3 biomes complete. Each biome will have a Main Quest as well as a number of side-quests. There will be Cities, Settlements, Ruins to explore, and tons of characters to meet. The 1.0 version of the game will have an additional biome that will have a Main Quest that wraps up the overall story and its own side-quests, locations, characters and hidden secrets as well. That 4th biome will likely be the largest in the game. We may also add additional locations beyond the 4th biome.

As we go through Early Access we know that we will build certain content, and I will post a road map for that at some point. We also plan on leaving space to be able to make more content that's driven by player demand. For us that's the main point of Early Access; to find out what player's like and give them more of it and then correct anything player's don't like. 

We're very excited to get people playing soon and we appreciate the patience. I will post another update again in a month. If there are any specific topics our questions you would like me to focus on please let me know. Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Open-World City Builder RPG
notes.notes:
Been a while since a devlog, but that doesn't mean that we've stopped working -- far from it! In fact, I've been so focused on actually making the game, it's been hard to justify spending the time to write a post! But approaching the end of the year feels like a good checkpoint to catch everyone up.

It's hard to summarize all the new things... so let's see...

These last few months has really seen the gameplay in Airborne Empire evolve drastically. The combat gameplay loop feels Very Good, testament to [b]Zach [/b]and all the time he's put into tuning the basic Defense Tower, Cannon, and Hangar mechanics. [b]Fred [/b]has also added a lot of functionality around workers repairing buildings and putting out fires. And my UI has finally caught up, allowing for better visibility into what you need to prioritize when your city is getting bombarded.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/9920a61ea0407d7fa792792c7926a6ebf2e86aee.png[/img]

At the same time, we've added a ton more content! [b]Amanda [/b]and the art team have created an entirely new biome -- an arid desert that evokes some elements from Airborne Kingdom while keeping this game's unique style. She's also gone back to our first biome and reworked the colors to keep the warm, cozy feel, but add vibrance to both land and sea. Even more ruins, treasures, and hidden secrets have been added.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/6a1a0f28d01460d4a920927a98c3cd80b1c9b4b2.png[/img]

And all the while [b]Dante[/b] and our portrait artist [b]Luke [/b] have been populating the increasingly huge landscape with character portraits and lots of quests. Our new portraits show off so much more personality, and I'm excited to showcase all the flair in our dialogue too!

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/8f607aed20c8c5e7694dec4b2b57797517da010d.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/7da2b8aa299de4f46b94b4dc4b02b878b36ea500.png[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/a876a8c1fbad5c8e968df912ce52d9537528bde5.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/d690bc7d8c917274e8da4a3c48a5004e9e29ef0b.png[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/5af7462df52d446f38fd06b9ab59e6dda02bfb83.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/29b18382661e858547fdfdae92f2339e4bbd03a9.png[/img][/url]

Altogether, this has made the true character of the game finally emerge. It doesn't quite feel like anything you've played before. You're more than flying over a landscape, you're discovering a world; you're daring fate and finding adventure; you're defeating enemies in myriad ways by making distinct upgrade choices.

What we have here is truly an [b]Open World City Builder RPG![/b]

It's pretty special... and I'm excited to share it with you next year!

notes.title: Devlog: Back from Montreal!
notes.notes:
No updates in the last couple of weeks, huh? Well we were busy! We all met up in lovely Montreal, Fred's homeland.

At least once a year, all our full-time dev-team members get together and work from the same space. Unfortunately BJ couldn't join us this time, but our part-time QA fella AJ tagged along instead, since the drive wasn't too far for him!

Here's all of us at work in Fred's living room:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/0512e8bf2adbefa18b1ced4ddb9b0c04882bf58f.jpg[/img]

What did we do? Well, plenty of playing the game! Up until now, Zach has been the main player on the team, but as more features come online, the more of us want to get our hands on it. We made some crucial balance changes, but mostly... we had fun with the game!

Maybe this doesn't make sense to those not in game-dev, but the game isn't always fun to play -- and usually, not right-away, immediately after many features come online. And yet, this one is! I'm sure it helps that we're building a sequel, on top of features that are already enjoyable. But even the new stuff -- the exploration, the massive world, the dialogue, and the combat -- all feel cohesive already! Kudos to Zach for all his playtime and design efforts: we have something good right now!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/6322403f64fef884aa0cc62f7df6fb6472de6395.jpg[/img]

Fred got lots of insights into both what to change in the current features and why he should change them. We also discussed the features currently not implemented, like the Attack Hangar ability, and where those might be useful.

Amanda and I also finally sat down and played with the world colors -- which involved changing a lot of our textures and materials and also tweaking the visual environments at various times of day. 

Here's a look at the latest; definitely not 100% final, but closer to what we want. Oh, and included in that screenshot is the new build bar I've now designed implemented in the game too!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/08bbe6d3faccb0a0972e57da6dd8b3febf94c5d5.png[/img]

Hope that's enough of a catch-up for now, to those eager for development updates. I'll get back to regular weekly ones next week!

notes.title: Devlog: So Much Gak!
notes.notes:
Hey followers, today let's talk about gak!

I love the idea of not just showing you something, but explaining why we have it, so let's try that now 🙂 

Gak is a term we borrowed from our old art director at Visceral Games, Ian Milham. If you search for the term, nothing related to our use comes up, so we'll have to ask him where he got it. 

It's become a part of Amanda's Art Bible, and to quote that document exactly, what we mean is "contrast of a few large shapes with a few mediums and lots [and lots and lots] of smaller details". Gak is all the girders hanging down, and the ropes swinging, and the random fins and propellers and gears and flaps and everything that just gives LIFE to the buildings.

Take a look at the base of our new Town Center in the screenshots below. On the left is Amanda's original blockout, and on the right is her adding tons of gak to it! See the difference?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44228604/46d06dd5f10958fd068ed46c1e520b55385017e9.png[/img]

We want players to feel like these are intricate, yet cobbled together pieces of technology. You look at something and can't exactly tell how it works, but all those pieces make it feel somehow just complicated enough that you believe it. "Mechanical Magic" is another term we keep coming back to.

Of course with this extra detail comes potentially lots of performance issues. So Amanda has to be judicious in her use of verts. But Fred is also deep in optimization land, making improvements to other areas of our GPU code so we can support many more details. And I have to make sure none of my own tech art is too expensive on the GPU too 😉 

It's really a team effort to get this look that we want, but it's led by Amanda's vision for the buildings in the sky. 

Hope that gives you some insight into what we're making! Let me know if you dig what we're doing here, or anything else you might want to know about, in the comments below. We'll share more in next week's devlog. 

Thanks for the support ❤️

notes.title: Devlog: Introducing the Team
notes.notes:
Hey all! Consider this the first Steam devlog update. I'll do these at least weekly, so keep tabs on Steam or on our [url=https://discord.gg/airbornekingdom]Discord[/url] if you'd like to know more! 

For now, I want to start by telling you about our team. Some members are here from [i]Airborne Kingdom[/i], but we have a few new faces too, and some of our roles have also changed! Consider this a wave hello from all of us!

I'll begin with myself. Last game, I did a lot of the design and all of the writing, as well as standing up the UI code. On this project, I've shifted roles a lot. I'm now doing all the tech art and rendering engineering, specifically around tweaking our rendering pipeline, writing custom shaders, creating our Visual Effects, and optimizing our GPU. I'm also wholly owning the UX Design and UI Implementation, which includes our new Dialogue tech. These are areas I have a lot of interest in, and I've learned quite a lot from working on our console ports -- enough that I know this is a full job for our follow-up! But then, who's designing the game...?

Much like the last game, it's ultimately a collaboration, but our captain for this voyage is Zach Mumbach. Last game he was our Producer and did a lot of the level design and world building, and much of our early QA. He's now picking up the big Systems Design mantle, and working out how our systems integrate and evolve with our new mechanics. Zach was so passionate about making this follow-up that it was hard to imagine another person helming the project. He has so many good ideas on mechanics and story, and it's exciting to see all of them getting implemented and written. Implemented by...?

Fred Gareau, our Tech Director Extraordinaire. His focus on this project has been quick turnarounds of new features, to give Zach lots of knobs to play with, as well as many many tech improvements -- to make our code more re-usable, maintainable, and much more efficient. While some of this stuff is very under-the-hood, there are plenty of tweaks that are easy to point to visually, like giving our Pirates really interesting flight paths, or adding arcs to our Cannon shots for better visibility. But while Fred can code, he can't write...

So we have Dante Douglas -- hey, the first new face! Dante's laying out the entire world lore right now! He and Zach are working on a story bible that we can pull interesting quests from. Something that gives our story history and depth. He'll also be the one actually writing the dialogue, too, which includes characters this time around, with their own goals and motivations. We'll see many different peoples in various cities and biomes, all made by...

BJ Timberlake - Art Warlock, our returning environment artist from Airborne Kingdom. Pretty much everything on the ground is his modeling -- the mines, the world geo, the rocks and various frills. He's already created the lookset for our starting region, which you can briefly see in our trailer, and now he's moving onto new biomes to explore. Places where you can find novel technologies, that lead to a variety of buildings once researched. Buildings made by...

Amanda Cheng -- another new friend! If BJ is making everything on the ground, Amanda is making everything in the sky. All the housing, production, lift, propulsion, morale, and many more categories of buildings flying through the air. That also includes all other flying objects too -- gather planes, enemy pirates... flying merchants??? Additionally, she's responsible for the overall cohesive look of the game. She's recently created an Art Bible, and has been adjusting post-processing effects, and tweaking any new materials or VFX I might give her to work with.  That's a lot of new stuff, all tested by...

AJ Fraser, our part-time tester and full-time cheerleader! He played hours upon hours of Airborne Kingdom, and now he has been passionately breaking all of our new features -- thankfully, before they're broken by all of you! He'll also be recording a lot of our #content for sharing on social media, so if you see a GIF you like across the internet, make sure you let him know!

Those are all the people touching the game on a daily basis, but of course there are a few more folks helping fly this big contraption. Paul Aubry is returning to compose another masterpiece soundtrack. FiftyCC will still be doing our PR, especially around big trailers and launch. And of course we have the fine folks from Stray Fawn helping publish the game -- everything from submitting to events, to handling a lot of our social media, to goosing those Steam numbers.

(Speaking of Steam, have you wishlisted yet?! If anyone hasn't, it would be really really helpful if you do!)

With so many folks doing so many things, it'll be difficult deciding what to post about every week! But I'll leave it here for now, this update is extra long. I promise the next one will be less of a text-wall and feature many more cool images.

For now, thanks again for being so supportive, and I'm happy to have y'all along with us as we fly towards Early Access next year!

notes.title: Get ready to balance your flying city and shoot down air pirates in Airborne Empire
notes.notes: City-building game Airborne Kingdom was a really new, interesting twist on the genre, challenging you to balance the growth of your flying city with its physical needs: Keep it balanced so it doesn't tip over, keep it agile enough to move forward, and keep it supplied with supplies from the surface. It also had a world to explore, with a real story, ending on a cliffhanger reveal that gave your flying city a new mission. It was a critically-acclaimed city builder in the sky... Read more.

notes.title: This city-building game is like Frostpunk, but in the sky
